articles.headline: Emi Martínez considering Argentina future after World Cup final heartbreak
articles.description: Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez is considering his international future after suffering the heartache of World Cup final defeat.

articles.headline: LaLiga president Javier Tebas blasts FIFA, calls on Gianni Infantino to resign
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has warned that expanding the World Cup to 64 teams would represent the continuing destruction of the football industry under FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who he called on to resign.

articles.headline: The players who played no minutes at the World Cup -- who were the unlucky few?
articles.description: The World Cup was a time to remember for most, for a handful of players though, their time at the tournament was merely sitting in the best seats in the house.

articles.headline: Enzo Fernández to 'keep giving his all' for Argentina after World Cup heartbreak
articles.description: Argentina's Enzo Fernández has said wearing his country's shirt is the "greatest honour" for him and has pledged to keep giving everything for the team following heartache in the World Cup final.

articles.headline: Gary Neville slams Argentina: 'Without Messi, they'd struggle to get to the semifinals'
articles.description: Gary Neville has sharply criticised Argentina's style of play in the World Cup final against Spain and is the latest pundit to slam Lionel Scaloni's men for their tactics.

articles.headline: Argentina, without Lionel Messi, greeted by fans in Buenos Aires after World Cup return
articles.description: Thousands of fans gathered in Buenos Aires on Monday evening to give a warm welcome to the Argentina football squad, who arrived home without captain Lionel Messi after their World Cup final loss to Spain.
